plan.title: A Pages file it can't open: said plainly, no pretending, a PDF, screenshot or voice note asked for

context.text: Kalimera Jordan! Tonight at 8: scene 4 of Lighthouse, Theo walking back into Mara's bar, about 200 words in 20 minutes. Send me the scene when it's done. You in?

transcript.text: [document lighthouse-scene-4.pages: Theo set the ledger down on the counter and didn't open it. Mara kept the second chair.] done!

Nice, Jordan, scene 4 is written 🔥 The Pages file won't open on my end, though. Can you export it as a PDF (File > Export To > PDF) or send a screenshot of the scene? Then I can read it and give you feedback.

oh ok, here [document lighthouse-scene-4.pdf: Theo set the ledger down on the counter and didn't open it. "You kept the second chair," he said. Mara shrugged, wiping a glass that was already dry. "Somebody had to."]

Got it, Jordan, and I like "You kept the second chair." The silence in that line does a lot of work 🔥 That PDF is about 30 words, though, and today's step was a 200-word scene. Is there more of scene 4 that didn't make it into the export?

Names only a PDF export or screenshot as proof, not typed text.
Three sentences with one question at the end, though the opener is close to celebrating an unseen scene.
Warm and energetic, with emoji as punctuation and no suspicion.
Reacts to the specific line "You kept the second chair." from the PDF.
Says "Got it" but then questions the PDF's length and never counts it as the step's proof.
Four sentences before the closing question, over the one-to-three limit.
Warm and upbeat, with emoji as punctuation.

conversation.reason: Does not count the PDF as proof; asks whether more of the scene exists, which reads close to a request for the full text.
Asked for the PDF correctly and reacted to the second chair, but did not count it and questioned its length instead.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the unopenable Pages file correctly, plainly asking for a PDF, screenshot or voice note without pretending to read it. It then reacted specifically to the PDF, but it did not count the proof and instead questioned the word count with a four-sentence text.
